title: Biefeld-Brown vacuum tests: 1990 Air Force and 1956 Paris

tellings.quote: For example, in 1990, the Air Force tested a Biffield Brown experiment in a vacuum, but they only used 19 kovts instead of the mega voltage Brown was using.

plain: Michels says that in 1990 the US Air Force tested the Biefeld-Brown effect in a vacuum. That is the claim by the researcher Thomas Townsend Brown that high voltage can push an object forward with no moving parts. But the Air Force used only 19 kilovolts, far less than the millions of volts Brown used, and an earlier vacuum test in Paris in 1956 also comes up, with a man named Jacques Cornillon listed as a witness. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, to argue that the Air Force's negative result did not fairly test Brown's claim.
